title: IAEA reports progress in Syria investigation, none in Iran
summary:
IAEA reports progress in Syria investigation, none in Iran

The UN nuclear watchdog has resolved its outstanding questions in its investigation into past, secret nuclear activities in Syria under the Assad family's rule, a confidential report by the agency seen by Reuters said on Tuesday.

A separate, quarterly International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) report on Iran also sent to member states and seen by Reuters showed there had again been no progress in Iran, where its lack of access to verify uranium stocks since US and Israeli attacks in June 2025 remained a "proliferation concern".

Reporting by Reuters

title: IRGC say US will 'regret' renewed attacks
summary:
IRGC say US will 'regret' renewed attacks

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has vowed that the US will "regret" its fresh attacks on the country, despite US President Donald Trump warning Tehran against striking back. 

"Severe punishment awaits the aggressors; the United States will regret its new attacks," spokesman Hossein Mohebi said in a post on X, after explosions were heard in multiple areas along and east of the Strait of Hormuz.  

Citing a senior Iranian military source, Tasnim news agency also reported that Iran will respond to US attacks with a response "several times larger", targeting US bases and interests in the region.

title: Trump warns of 'much harder' action if Iran retaliates after strikes
summary:
Trump warns of 'much harder' action if Iran retaliates after strikes

US President Donald Trump has warned that Iran will face "much harder and higher" attacks if it hits back against what he called "very justified" US strikes on the country.

"If the failed Nation of Iran retaliates for this very justified attack, they will be hit again at a much harder and higher level, but it will not be the biggest attack of them all, that is waiting in the wings and, when it is over, there will be very little left of the Islamic Republic of Iran!" Trump said on his Truth Social network.

He added that the strikes were in response to Iran laying mines and shooting missiles at an American base in Jordan.

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: US army secretary resigns amid signs of Pentagon unease with Iran war
summary:
US army secretary resigns amid signs of Pentagon unease with Iran war

Submitted by MEE staff on Tue, 09/01/2026 - 17:58
Dan Driscoll was a close ally of Vice President JD Vance but clashed with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth
US Secretary of the Army Dan Driscoll testifies during a House budget hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington on 16 April 2026 (Saul Loeb/AFP)
Off

The US Army's top civilian leader, Dan Driscoll, has submitted his resignation, the White House confirmed on Monday, following reports of tensions with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.

"Driscoll has been highly effective in advancing President Trump's agenda to Make America Strong Again at the Department of the Army," Anna Kelly, the White House deputy press secretary, said in a statement on Monday.

"The United States Army is more powerful than ever thanks to his work alongside the Commander-in-Chief and Secretary of War,” she added.

Driscoll’s departure comes at a time of signs there is unease in the Pentagon over how the Trump administration is prosecuting the war on Iran.

The heads of the army, navy and air force, and the four-star commanders overseeing US operations throughout Europe, Asia and Latin America, warned Hegseth that any prolonging of major operations would weaken the US’s ability to confront other foes, the Washington Post reported on Monday.

The Associated Press reported earlier this month that the war on Iran has caused a "beyond critical" shortage of advanced missile interceptors, especially Patriots, which have been used to shoot down Russian ballistic missiles in the Ukraine war.

The US has also exhausted its stockpile of sophisticated long-range missiles and has “virtually" used up its supply of surface-to-surface weapons, including ATACMS and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM), Reuters reported.

An army veteran who served in Iraq, Driscoll ran unsuccessfully for Congress in 2020 and later advised Trump's 2024 re-election campaign. He was an ally of General Randy George, the army chief of staff fired by Hegseth in April. While he has reportedly clashed with the former, he was seen as benefiting from his ties to former law school classmate, Vice President JD Vance.

'No end in sight': Democrats slam Trump after six months of Iran war
Read More »

Vance is seen as standing on the isolationist wing of the Republican Party. He took a visible lead negotiating with Iran in the springtime, in talks hosted by Pakistan in Islamabad. In July, he accused Israel of “manipulating” US public opinion in a bid to keep the war going.

Hegseth, in contrast, has emerged as one of the most visible defenders of the war, giving feisty press conferences where he has scolded journalists about their coverage of the conflict.

Vance is widely considered to be a 2028 presidential hopeful, along with Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Middle East Eye reported in March that Rubio and Hegseth were described as “at each other's throats” over the question of whether the US should deploy troops to Iran at Israel’s request. Hegseth was supportive of the position at the time, while Rubio was wary of entangling the US in a long war, the sources told MEE.

Driscoll’s departure effectively leaves the army without permanent civilian or uniformed leadership as the Iran war grinds into its seventh month.

title: Iran says four projectiles hit cities east of Hormuz Strait
summary:
Iran says four projectiles hit cities east of Hormuz Strait

The deputy governor for security and law enforcement in Iran’s Sistan and Baluchestan province said on Tuesday that four projectiles struck the southeastern cities of Chabahar and Konarak, east of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's IRNA news agency. He added that assessments of possible damage are under way.

Iran’s Fars news agency also reported that several explosions were heard in Konarak, while the exact location remains unclear, following earlier reports of explosions heard east of Bandar Abbas.

The US military announced on Tuesday that it was carrying out new strikes on Iran.

title: WHO raises concerns over amputees and deteriorating water quality in Gaza
summary:
WHO raises concerns over amputees and deteriorating water quality in Gaza

The World Health Organization (WHO) on Tuesday raised concerns about deteriorating water quality, contamination and subsequent disease risks in the genocide-stricken Gaza Strip ahead of the upcoming winter.

Addressing reporters from Gaza, Reinhilde Van de Weerdt, WHO representative for the occupied Palestinian territories, stated that “between January and August this year, over 6,700 water samples had been tested, and microbiological contamination almost tripled, from under six percent in January to over 18 percent in August”.

She noted that “there had been a significant increase in cases of Acute Watery Diarrhoea over the same period, when cases nearly doubled”.

"Sewage, waste, and contaminated water would not stay where they were, they would spread into the very spaces where people sleep, cook, and care for their children, furthering the risk and spread of waterborne diseases,” she added. 

Van de Weerdt stressed the importance of permanent shelters, suitable provision of water and waste management.

She also highlighted the lack of access to essential services for amputees, noting that 6,600 people required long-term care for limb amputations, but prosthetic limbs had not been allowed into Gaza since May 2024.

As of July 2026, only 12 percent of 4,600 patients who lost limbs since October 2023 had been fitted with a prosthetic device, she added.
